1: Chapter 1: A Visitor on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Peñaseca for three days. In spring, Lucía Romero's older sister had left for Madrid, and ever since, Lucía had been running the village's small apothecary alone.
When night fell, she closed the shutters, counted what she had earned that day, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when someone knocked hard on the door downstairs. A man's voice asked, "Is anyone there?"
On the threshold stood a young man soaked to the bone, his left arm wrapped in a cloth stained with blood. He said his name was Diego Lobo and that he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need you to heal me," said Lobo in a low voice. "I can pay. Would three thousand five hundred reals be enough?"
He pulled a letter wrapped in waxed paper from his jacket. "This letter has to reach the monastery of San Blas before May eighteenth."
For Lucía, healing that wound was a piece of cake, but the letter worried her.
Even so, she did not accept his money and only said, "Tomorrow at dawn I will take it to the mountain."
2: At dawn they set out. Lucía carried a basket on her back with bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the slope they met old Tomás Gil, who was chopping wood. He put down his axe and told them in a low voice that the previous afternoon three strangers had asked at the village entrance about a wounded young man.
"Take the path, Lucía," said Tomás Gil. "The main road is not safe." Lucía thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Lucía walked ahead, planting her foot firmly with each step. Lobo followed her in silence.
At noon the rain stopped, the fog lifted slowly, and in the distance the roof of the San Blas monastery appeared. A nun, Sister Inés, waited at the door, in charge of receiving visitors.
Sister Inés took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting 2 years for this letter."
Lobo said to Lucía, "I owe you my life." Lucía smiled. "Then the next time you come, fix the roof of the apothecary." Lobo stayed at the monastery.
At dusk Lucía descended the mountain alone. When she arrived home it was already night; she lit the lamp and sat for a long time behind the counter.
